licence noun

an official permit

also license, permit, work permit, residence permit

classical

Plin. Ep. 10.46
Cic. Att. 10.17.4 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 217

diplōma, diplōmatis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a licence, a permit (the document)

A document from a magistrate assuring its holder some right or favour (Lewis & Short); in Pliny’s letters to Trajan, the permits for travelling by the public post. Traupman uses it for a driving licence (see driving licence); the passport is commeātūs diplōma (see passport).

Other words

  • licentia, licentiae f. — leave, permission; in Neo-Latin a licence

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.103: puerīs nōn omnem lūdendī licentiam damus; M-O s.v. driver’s license; city council · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically the freedom to do as one pleases, given or taken, and often too much of it (Lewis & Short). Morgan–Owens records it for a licence in Neo-Latin: licentiam ad tabernam coffeāriam condendam, a licence to open a coffee house (Trappen, 1843).

Examples

  • Diplōmata, quōrum praeteritus est diēs, nōn dēbent esse in ūsū.

    Permits whose date has passed should not be used.Plin. Ep. 10.46

See also driving licence, passport, allow, form.
